title: error-debugging-inspector-mockups
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures notes, low-fi wireframes, and a prioritized grooming backlog for a new Console view: the Error Debugging Inspector. Goal is to give engineers (SRE, ML infra, platform) a single-pane workflow to triage request failures (timeouts, 5xx, model errors) and take fast remediation actions (rerun, fallback, escalate).

Context & problem statement:
- Customers and internal SREs frequently open support tickets when production requests return 5xx, timeouts, or model exceptions. Current console requires jumping between traces, logs, and model catalog pages.
- Key gaps: no unified per-request failure summary, poor visibility into model-side error codes (OOM, NaN, tokenization failures), and limited quick-action controls (reroute to variant, replay with different timeout).

Primary users / personas:
- Platform engineer: needs root cause signals (hardware, kernel failure, memory pressure) to decide capacity actions.
- ML engineer: needs model-level failures (invalid logits, length-exceeded, tokenization mismatch) and ability to compare outputs across model variants.
- SRE / Support: needs concise timeline and a single-button way to rerun or attach a support bundle for a ticket.

User goals (ranked):
1) Quickly determine whether failure is client, network, runtime, or model.
2) See a per-request breakdown (latency, time spent in queue, kernel, KV fetch).
3) Replay the request with variant model/quantization/profile and compare outputs.
4) Surface correlated failures across time (spike detection) and route to fallback models automatically.

High-level design principles:
- Single-pane first: summary + timeline + inspector details in vertically stacked cards.
- Actionable defaults: show most-likely cause heuristically (e.g., latency > SLO & kernel error => runtime).
- Lightweight trace snippets: avoid overloading with full logs; show contextual snippets and link to full trace.
- Keep privacy: redact user tokens/PII in request preview; surface only hashed inputs.

Proposed UI components (order = top -> bottom):
1) Header bar (fixed): request id, timestamp, status badge (timeout / 5xx / model-error), primary action buttons (Rerun, Route to fallback, Create support bundle).
2) Summary card: one-line cause guess, key metrics (end-to-end latency, model latency, token count, response tokens, backend host), small trend sparkline for same error over last 30m.
3) Timeline waterfall: stacked bars showing queue -> kernel -> model forward -> KV fetch -> response serialization. Hover shows ms and percent. Color segments red/orange when anomalous.
4) Error diagnostic panel (tabs):
   - Runtime (5xx, OOM, kernel panic) => stack trace snippet, GPU memory snapshot, node id, driver version, recent kernel logs link.
   - Network (timeout, connection reset) => upstream host, RTT histogram, proxy logs snippet.
   - Model (NaN, tokenization error, invalid logits) => model name + version, failure code, model logs, last successful checkpoint, token sequence around failure, top-k logits where available.
   - Client (bad request, unsupported content) => client sdk, sdk version, example payload (redacted), schema diff.
5) Request inspector: full (redacted) input, prompt template mapping (if applicable), tool calls captured, function-call outputs, response partials. Offer copy-to-playground.
6) Output compare pane (collapsible): allow replay with up to 2 alternate model variants side-by-side. Show delta of tokens and log-prob differences.
7) Correlated events list: similar request ids (same error code, same model variant, same host) with quick filters (last 5m, last 1h).
8) Actions footer: Rerun (with modal to pick model/timeout), Route (choose fallback policy), Pin as incident, Create support bundle (collect logs + full trace + model weights diff), Annotate.

Low-fidelity wireframe notes (visual layout):
- Top 60px header: request id | status badge | action buttons (Rerun, Route, Bundle)
- Left column (60%): Summary card -> Timeline -> Request inspector -> Output compare
- Right column (40%): Error diagnostic panel (tabbed) -> Correlated events -> Quick metrics (CPU/GPU/Memory at time)
- Actions footer sticky at bottom for the session

Example mockup flows (three common cases):
A) Timeout (end-to-end > SLO):
   - Summary: "Probable runtime saturation (queue 85% of total)."
   - Timeline: long queue + small kernel time.
   - Diagnostic: Node CPU at 98%, queue backlog peaked. Show autoscaler events (if any).
   - Suggested actions: reroute to dedicated pool, increase timeout and rerun, add to incident.
B) 5xx (model runtime crash / OOM):
   - Summary: "Model runtime OOM (GPU mem spike)."
   - Diagnostic:model tab shows OOM trace, memory dump pointer, model size and quantization.
   - Suggested actions: rerun on variant quantized or smaller context window; flag for model onboarding team.
C) Model error (tokenization or generation exception):
   - Summary: "Model error: tokenization mismatch at token index 234."
   - Diagnostic: show offending token sequence, raw bytes, tokenizer version mismatch.
   - Suggested actions: Replay with alternative tokenizer or sanitize input, escalate to model owner.

Backlog / grooming items (prioritized):
- [P0] request-inspector-core: Build header + summary + timeline visualization. Owner: Evan. Est: 5d. Acceptance: single request view with timeline + cause guess + rerun modal. Linked: JIRA-PI-942.
- [P0] error-tab-model: Model diagnostics tab showing failure codes, tokenization snippets, and model meta. Owner: Priya. Est: 4d. Acceptance: displays model error details for 80% of model-errors in recent logs. Linked: JIRA-OPS-317.
- [P1] correlated-events-index: backend index to return similar request ids by hash/time. Owner: Riley. Est: 3d. Acceptance: returns top 10 correlated events in <500ms.
- [P1] output-compare: Rerun with 2 alternate variants and show token diffs. Owner: Aisha. Est: 5d. Acceptance: side-by-side outputs with basic diff highlighting.
- [P2] support-bundle: one-button bundle generation (logs + trace + model-meta + config). Owner: infra-support. Est: 4d.
- [P2] autosuggest-actions: heuristics that recommend action buttons (e.g., reroute if node busy). Owner: ml-infra. Est: 3d.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- To what extent do we surface full stack traces vs snippets? (privacy + noise). Proposal: snippets + link to full logs with RBAC gating.
- Should rerun default to same model variant or to a heuristic fallback? Lean default = same model but UI suggests fallback if runtime OOM or node saturated.
- Storage/perf: correlated events query could be heavy. Need bloom-filtering or precomputed error signatures.

Privacy & security note:
- Support bundle must redact PII and user secrets. We need an allowlist of fields to collect. No raw user prompts in bundles without owner consent.

Prototype tasks (next 2 sprints):
1) Sketch final V1 wireframe in Figma (Riley) — include component tokens for timeline + diff view.
2) Implement mock data API (Evan) to drive timeline + diagnostics panel.
3) Backend: error-signature index + small query service (Riley & infra).
4) UX validation session with 3 customers + internal SRE rotation.

Notes to self / rough TODOs:
- Add keyboard shortcut for "Rerun with fallback" (cmd+shift+r).
- Investigate exposing kernel version and driver on runtime diag (security review required).
- Create template for support bundle email body.

References / links:
- Slack: #console-debugging (prototype channel)
- Related tickets: JIRA-PI-942, JIRA-OPS-317
- Prototype PR: github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/218

Status: draft — ready for internal grooming (product + eng + SRE).

Unresolved: prioritization between output-compare and model diagnostics. Recommend shipping diagnostics + timeline first (P0) and output-compare in P1.
